name: Differential Privacy
description: Differentially private mechanisms, analytics, and deployments, including local DP.
narrative:
The earliest papers in this list, all from 2018, mark differential privacy's transition from theory to deployable systems and tooling. On the local DP (LDP) side, where users perturb their own data before sending it to an untrusted collector, "Locally Differentially Private Frequent Itemset Mining" (S&P 2018) and "CALM: Consistent Adaptive Local Marginal for Marginal Release under Local Differential Privacy" (CCS 2018) pushed LDP beyond simple frequency estimation toward richer analytics like itemsets and marginals. In parallel, a verification thread emerged: "Detecting Violations of Differential Privacy" (CCS 2018) and "DP-Finder" (CCS 2018) attacked the problem that the sophisticated mechanisms being published were often buggy, building tools to find privacy violations automatically.

Around 2019, the center of gravity shifted toward machine learning. "Evaluating Differentially Private Machine Learning in Practice" (USENIX 2019) became a touchstone by showing how loosely the privacy budget epsilon was being interpreted, while "Differentially Private Model Publishing for Deep Learning" (S&P 2019) and "Towards Practical Differentially Private Convex Optimization" (S&P 2019) worked on making private training usable. A striking cross-over result, "Certified Robustness to Adversarial Examples with Differential Privacy" (S&P 2019), repurposed DP machinery for adversarial robustness rather than privacy itself. LDP analytics kept maturing too, with "PrivKV" (S&P 2019) extending collection to key-value data.

The 2020-2021 period brought two complementary maturations: scaling the theory and stress-testing the guarantees. The shuffle model emerged as a middle ground between local and central DP, studied in "Private Summation in the Multi-Message Shuffle Model" (CCS 2020) and "On the Rényi Differential Privacy of the Shuffle Model" (CCS 2021). At the same time, an adversarial-auditing line questioned whether deployed DP actually delivered: "Adversary Instantiation: Lower Bounds for Differentially Private Machine Learning" (S&P 2021) empirically probed DP-SGD's real leakage, "Manipulation Attacks in Local Differential Privacy" (S&P 2021) showed malicious users could skew LDP aggregates, and "DP-Sniper" (S&P 2021) automated black-box discovery of violations. A human-factors thread also opened, asking what users actually understand, in "I need a better description: An Investigation Into User Expectations For Differential Privacy" (CCS 2021).

By 2022-2024 the field had become self-critical and application-driven. "Are We There Yet? Timing and Floating-Point Attacks on Differential Privacy Systems" (S&P 2022) showed that even correct math leaks through implementation side channels, continuing the auditing lineage. DP moved into modern ML deployments through "DP-Forward" (CCS 2023) for language models and "PrivateFL" (USENIX 2023) for federated learning, while usability work matured with "What Are the Chances? Explaining the Epsilon Parameter in Differential Privacy" (USENIX 2023). Finally, consolidating SoKs like "SoK: Privacy-Preserving Data Synthesis" (S&P 2024) signal a field that now spans rigorous mechanisms, real-world systems, attacks, and human comprehension.
